critical_code_review_comments: shares.py: allowed_types is a function-local set rebuilt on every request — fine for 6 types, but if it grows consider hoisting to a module constant for readability and so the 400-detail list is generated from a single source of truth.
shares.py: `period` is free-form Optional[str] and not length-capped — a client could POST a 100KB period value that gets stored verbatim. Low-risk (auth-gated) but worth Field(max_length=128).

shares.py: no index on shares.{user_id, share_type, created_at} — the /admin/shares/stats aggregation will scan the full collection as the table grows. Add a compound index when share volume is non-trivial.

shares.py: share is fire-and-forget per the docstring, but failure modes (db.shares.insert_one raising) bubble up as 500 rather than the intended non-blocking behaviour. If the client is supposed to treat this endpoint as best-effort, wrap the insert in try/except and still return {success: true} (or a distinct 202).

shares.py routing: `/admin/shares/stats` lives inside the shares router but is an admin concern — keeps test coverage tight, just confirm this is consistent with how other admin/* routes are mounted (no prefix mismatch).
